instantiated_cells.justification: The law prohibits engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist without being licensed and authorized (§13.66), and defines a ‘lobbyist’ as an individual paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying (with a 5-days-per-reporting-period threshold if duties are mixed) (§13.62(11)).
Lobbyists must obtain a license to act as a lobbyist, and the license ‘shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year,’ requiring renewal biennially rather than at least once per year.
Lobbyists must file a license application to be issued a lobbyist license (§13.63), while principals must separately file a registration statement when they exceed the $500 threshold (§13.64).
The lobbyist license application must include specified items (e.g., signature and generally a social security number) but the statute does not require submission of a photograph.

An agency that files a statement under §13.695 and named officials are not subject to multiple lobbying provisions (§13.621(2)), and elective state officials, local/tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to listed lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity (§13.621(3)).

State agencies that file statements under §13.695 (and named officials) are expressly not subject to several requirements that apply to non-government actors (e.g., licensing/registration/reporting provisions) except as provided in §13.695 (§13.621(2)).

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections do not state any lobbyist-side deadline to notify the commission of changes in license/registration information; the only explicit change-notice rule provided is for agencies under §13.695(2).

The statute imposes a ‘before engaging’ licensing/authorization requirement (§13.66) but does not provide a numeric number-of-days-after-first-lobbying deadline for the lobbyist’s own registration/licensing.
